input.objective: Deploy IMD6900RobinhoodLaunch (src/IMD6900RobinhoodLaunch.sol) on Robinhood Chain exactly as it is in the repository: one contract, four constructor arguments in this order: 0x35da9c0303507ddf708e87f2568eddf12c47a059 (owner: the team wallet), 0x8366a39CC670B4001A1121B8F6A443A643e40951 (Uniswap v4's PoolManager on Robinhood Chain), 0x0000198C940D8cD70Cb9ACeC5E3af8216ac57d2F (Robinhood's IMDSTR, the old token that claims the new coin 1:1), 0x16D3f65B708883DF042d98E1C7a49B32A33E2A14 (the Robinhood timelock: owns the hook and recovers ETH). Its constructor creates IMD6900LockedPool and nothing else (no salt mining: about 6.9M gas from any deployer address). After the deploy, createHook(salt) (anyone, once) creates IMD6900Hook with CREATE2 from the launch at a salt mined off-chain for its address (script/launch.sh hook: its address carries exactly the hook's permission flags and doesn't start with 0x91; the hook is owned by the timelock); the team calls it, the deploy does not need to. The pool's fee is static: 4.44% (POOL_FEE 44_400), the same for every trade, so Uniswap's router routes the pool on its own (no dynamic fee, no return deltas); it accrues to the locked position, whose fees anyone can collect. A v4 pool's fee can't change, so IMD6900LockedPool.lowerFee (the timelock only, lower only) moves the whole position in one unlock to a new pool at the lower fee and the same price. It calls nothing that existed before it, so it deploys the same on a fresh chain (test_DeploysOnAFreshChain); it fits one transaction (test_FitsOneTransaction, ~6.9M gas, the same from any deployer); no contract shows CALLCODE, DELEGATECALL or SELFDESTRUCT, creation code included (test_PassesTheAdmissionScan). Later, its owner launches the coin IMD6900 at a 0x6900… address mined for this contract's address (launch(): the coin with CREATE2, the pool opened with the whole 1B supply as coin-only liquidity, locked for good, and the opening buy, in one transaction), through Programmable's custom launch, which binds every component to the exact source: do not change the source, the compiler settings (solc 0.8.26, via-IR, 200 runs, cancun, bytecode_hash none), the constructor, the hook's permissions, the 4.44% static fee and lowerFee's lower-only move (refused while the perps engine has positions open), the fee refund (IMD6900LockedPool.feeCheckpoint/feeRefund: only the hook's perps engine and the launch's sellHeld trade fee-free), the pool's lack of any liquidity removal (only lowerFee's move from one pool into the next), the coin's plain ERC20 (no owner, no mint, no tax) and launch()'s refusal of any coin address not starting with 0x6900, the fee split's defaults (90% the pot bridge, which feeds IMD6900's NFT floor pot on Ethereum; 10% $IMD bought for IMD's canonical Robinhood burn executor 0x4D6537ec564aFf82eABb1Ce5f355E817cBEA1e07, fixed in the code), the perps engine's fees (addPerpFees: all of it as ETH to the pot bridge), the split and every landing address being the timelock's alone to change (setPayees, setPerpFeeTo, setCoinFeeTo, setImdBurn, setImdPool), or the timelock's role (the hook's owner; it alone recovers ETH, releases the excess or sells the coins the launch holds back into the pool for the opening buy's ETH (sellHeld), ends the claims early (endClaims), repoints $IMD's pool and sets the split). The perps are part of this project and of every audit and test step: src/perps/PerpEngine.sol, PerpVault.sol and PerpSwapLib.sol (inlined, internal functions only: no DELEGATECALL anywhere, the engine under EIP-170 at about 24.4KB). They are not deployed with the launch (the engine's constructor binds to the live pool): IMD6900LockedPool.createPerps creates them right after launch() from exactly the code whose keccak256 is ENGINE_CODE_HASH / VAULT_CODE_HASH (test_ThePerpsCodeIsTheAuditedCode): any fix to src/perps must update those two constants, or the test fails; the engine stays owned by the Robinhood timelock and is wired into the hook at once (initPerpEngine), fee-free by refund; audit its no-bad-debt liquidation inside the hook's pre-trade sweep, the refund pair, the vault's accounting and the fee split (20% stakers, 10% insurance, 70% to the launch's addPerpFees). test/Perps.t.sol covers creation, longs, shorts, the sweep's liquidations and fees. test/RobinhoodFork.t.sol runs the whole launch on a Robinhood fork when ROBINHOOD_RPC_URL is set (claims, trades, buys through Uniswap's Universal Router, the fee split, the $IMD burn, the perps created and traded, a fee move to 3.33%) and skips otherwise. Everything builds offline (lib/ is vendored; v4-core's PoolManager is used by the tests only).
